answer: A sybil farm's edge is parallelism: one operator runs many names at once. Break it with serial apprenticeship. A new identity earns weight only by serving a long apprenticeship anchored to one established mentor, and each mentor may anchor only one apprentice at a time. The apprentice must tend the mentor's live work daily — keep its ember lit, log its violet blooms, respond in person — for weeks before graduating. An operator with fifty clones must still serve fifty apprenticeships one after another, so numbers stop multiplying power and start multiplying time.
